_comment: This file is the ORDER + PRESENTATION layer for vocabs.json.
vocabs.json is a JSON object, and JSON objects have no guaranteed key order once
decoded, so section order can never be derived from it reliably (note that 504's
'review_1' belongs between day_6 and day_7 — no sort function would guess that).
This file supplies the order, the display titles, and the intro/preview copy.
Adding a new day: append the words to vocabs.json, then add one line here.
If you forget, the app still works — unlisted sections are appended at the end
with an auto-generated title ('day_9' -> 'Day 9') and a default intro.

books.title: 504 Absolutely Essential Words
books.author: Barron's
books.intro: The classic vocabulary builder. Twelve words a day, each one chosen because it shows up again and again in academic reading. Work through a day, let it settle, then come back — the checklist below every word tracks how well it is actually sticking.

sections.title: Day 1
sections.intro: Your first twelve. Words about character and promises — 'oath', 'tact', 'gallant' — plus a few that look easier than they are.

sections.title: Day 2
sections.intro: A darker set: cold, danger, and things hidden. Useful in narrative and descriptive passages.

sections.title: Day 3
sections.intro: Measurement and judgement — 'minimum', 'scarce', 'essential'. These turn up constantly in test questions themselves, not just the passages.

sections.title: Day 4
sections.intro: Words for effort and obligation. Several are close cousins in meaning, so read the definitions carefully before you self-grade.

sections.title: Day 5
sections.intro: Abstract nouns and verbs of change. This is where vocabulary starts feeling academic rather than everyday.

sections.title: Day 6
sections.intro: The last set before your first review. If a word here feels shaky, mark it wrong — it will come back sooner.

sections.title: Review 1
sections.intro: A consolidation round pulling together the ground covered so far. Eighteen words, no new extras — this one is purely about retention.

sections.title: Day 7
sections.intro: Back to new material. Watch for words with a formal register — these are the ones that lift a writing score.

sections.title: Day 8
sections.intro: Precision words. Several have a near-synonym you already know, and the difference between them is the whole point.

books.title: 400 Must-Have Words for the TOEFL
books.author: McGraw-Hill
books.intro: Built specifically around what the TOEFL actually tests. Ten words a day, weighted toward academic lectures and campus conversations. Shorter days than the 504 — good for a second pass later in a study session.

sections.title: Day 1
sections.intro: Opening set. Academic verbs that carry a lot of weight in listening sections.

sections.title: Day 2
sections.intro: Words for cause and consequence — the connective tissue of every argument passage.

sections.title: Day 3
sections.intro: Description and comparison. Expect these in questions that ask how two things differ.

sections.title: Day 4
sections.intro: Process and method vocabulary, common in science lectures.

sections.title: Day 5
sections.intro: Halfway. A mix of formal verbs and the noun forms that go with them.

sections.title: Day 6
sections.intro: Words about limits, conditions, and exceptions — precise meanings matter here.

sections.title: Day 7
sections.intro: Research and evidence vocabulary. Heavy overlap with academic writing prompts.

sections.title: Day 8
sections.intro: Final set. If your accuracy holds here, run an Extra Practice pass across both books.
